I am 54, been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I only went to primary school, so I don't know much from books, but I know my fields. My son and daughter-in-law work in the factory in Handan, so it's mostly me and my husband doing the farm work, though they come back to help at harvest time.

This year I'll keep the same layout as last year: 4 mu cotton, 3 mu maize, and 1 mu mungbean. I thought about planting less cotton because picking hurts my back, but cotton still pays the best per mu, so I keep it.

For cotton, I use guoxinmian seeds — that's what Aunt Li down the road plants, and her cotton always grows well. The seed dealer in town says it's an improved variety. I till the soil with the rotary tiller in mid-April before planting. For fertilizer, I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that's 50 kg of the 15-15-15 kind. When the cotton starts flowering, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. I know fertilizer is expensive this year, but if the bolls don't fill out, I lose everything. I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. I irrigate three times from our well: once at flowering, once when the bolls are forming, and once in August if it's dry. Cotton worms are the biggest problem. Last year I sprayed 12 times for insects, plus one time for weeds. This year I'll do 13 sprays total. Last year I got about 600 jin of seed cotton per mu. If the weather is good, I hope for the same.

For maize, I plant denghai 605 hybrid seeds. Everyone in the village uses it. I don't till for maize — in June, right after we clear the field, I sow directly into the stubble. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu is enough for the base, and when the plants are knee-high, I topdress with about 20 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once after sowing if it doesn't rain, and once during the big growth period. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice, so three times total. I expect about 1200 jin per mu.

For mungbean on my 1 mu plot, I use my own saved seeds, the local kind. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and that's all. I irrigate twice if the rain is not enough. If I see bugs, I spray once or twice. I don't expect much — maybe 100 jin per mu — but mungbean is cheap to grow and the price was fine last year.

Everything costs more this year — fertilizer, pesticide, diesel for the pump. But I won't cut back on cotton or maize. Those are my main income. For mungbean, I keep it simple since it's only one mu.
